score_geometry_20261009.mathematical_criterion: For n=15 proofs all with 100% survival, +1 sum-of-two-axes objective point on one problem produces +1/45 ≈ 0.02222 combined portfolio points.
score_geometry_20261009.deduction: If only the six weak targets change, gains on at least four are mathematically necessary even at impossible perfect-axis limits. The one-axis-per-target best-case total is only 4.85 objective points above the 343.82 required, so optimizing one axis alone is not a credible strategy. Favor structural proof substitutions that jointly improve length and heartbeats, or cheap gains on any of the other nine proofs. Typing has nearly saturated heartbeat savings (96.35%) and needs large length reduction; SKI and Strata also primarily need length; Wick and Electromagnetism need both; Fiberwise has more heartbeat than length headroom.
score_geometry_20261009.cost_sanity: Seven one-lemma deletions of the 568-token public Wick proof are diagnostic probes, not plausibly enough to close a 343.82-point objective deficit.
score_geometry_20261009.promotion_boundary: Statement intact, compiled, no forbidden constructs or extra declarations, all required Lean versions, comparable official objective gain, then recompute 15-target score.
